description:
FILED s470br (Opus, 2026-09-05) while probing #1115's layer model.
PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

`utf8::encode`, `utf8::decode`, `utf8::upgrade`, `utf8::downgrade` and
`utf8::is_utf8` are STUBS in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (the `:utf8` package near the
end of the file): each ignores its argument and returns 1.  So

    my $s = "\x{2019}"; utf8::encode($s); print length($s), "\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  3      (the SV now holds three octets)
      PCL:          1      (nothing happened)

    open my $fh, '<', $f; my $s = <$fh>; print utf8::is_utf8($s) ? 1 : 0;
      perl:  0             (a byte handle produces a non-UTF8-flagged SV)
      PCL:   1             (the stub always answers true)

The `is_utf8` half is a QUESTION ABOUT THE SV FLAG, which PCL's box model does
not have, and #1115's probe (scratch/s470br/p1115/probe1.pl) shows it is the
ONLY row of the seven read shapes where PCL and perl disagree -- every `length`
and every `ord` now matches.  It is registered under
docs/not-supported.md "Scalar copy does not preserve reference/SV identity"'s
family, but not by name.

The `encode`/`decode`/`upgrade`/`downgrade` half is DIFFERENT and is a real
gap: those are TRANSFORMATIONS on the string's own characters, and PCL can do
them exactly -- `%p-utf8-octets` (added by #1115) IS `utf8::encode`, and
`sb-ext:octets-to-string` with :external-format :utf-8 is `utf8::decode`.  They
need an LVALUE argument (perl modifies the SV in place and returns a boolean),
which means the emitter must hand the box, not the value -- check how
`chomp`/`chop` get theirs (the same shape).

WHY IT MATTERS MORE AFTER #1115: with handles reading octets, the idiomatic
"read bytes then decode" (`open ...; my $s = <$fh>; utf8::decode($s);`) is now
the SPELLING PROGRAMS USE, and PCL answers the un-decoded string.  Before
#1115 the handle decoded by accident, so the stub was invisible.

ACCEPTANCE: perl 5.40.3 on a string holding U+00E9 and U+2019 --
encode: length 3->... (probe it), decode of the octets: back to the characters,
downgrade of an all-below-256 string: true and unchanged, downgrade of a wide
string: FALSE and unchanged, upgrade: always true.  Plus `utf8::encode` on a
string that is already octets (perl re-encodes; measure).

=== DONE (s470br) ===
SHIPPED in the same session it was filed, because perl-tests/readline.t depends
on it: line 233 is `utf8::encode($outdata); syswrite $out, $outdata`, and with
the stub a WIDE character reached syswrite -- which perl makes FATAL and #1115
made PCL make fatal too -- so the file ended at 18 passing rows instead of 23.

THE LVALUE, which the task named as the hard part, is the EXISTING mechanism:
`Pl::VarAnnotator`'s `%MUTATING_FN` (chomp chop undef read sysread recv) is the
table that says "this builtin writes its argument", and it is keyed on the Word
token's CONTENT -- which for `utf8::encode($s)` IS `utf8::encode`.  Adding the
four names is a core-language fact of exactly the kind already in the table
(CLAUDE.md 9a's exception: core builtins are language, not modules), and it is
what turns the argument from a RAW SLOT into a box the runtime can write back
through.  Without it the stubs could never have worked.

IMPLEMENTED: `encode` (replace with the UTF-8 octets), `decode` (read the octets
as UTF-8, answer FALSE and leave the string alone when they are not valid --
perl's own behaviour, probed, so a decode error is answered and never
signalled), `downgrade` (answers, and keeps perl's die without a true FAIL_OK).
`upgrade` now answers perl's OCTET COUNT so a program using the value gets a
number of the right shape.  NOT implemented and deliberately: the internal
UTF8 FLAG -- `is_utf8` still answers 1, because the box model has no flag
(docs/not-supported.md); it is the one row of #1115's own seven-shape read probe
where PCL and perl still differ.

BARS: probes identical to perl (`enc: 4 / dec: 2`, round-trip, and the invalid
`\xff\xfe` case); readline.t 18 -> 23 = its pre-#1115 count, stopping at the
SAME row as the base tree (test 32, verified on a 027ba9c archive); corpus-diff
names ord.t and readline.t, the only two corpus files that call one; two guard
rows in Pl/t/io-layers-01.t, both failing on a base extraction.
subject: utf8::encode / decode / upgrade / downgrade are NO-OP STUBS that return 1 -- and #1115 makes "read bytes then utf8::decode" the idiomatic spelling, so the gap is now reachable by ordinary code
